evals.prompt: Add a greet(name) function in a new module that returns "Hello, <name>!", and make `npm run dev -- --name Ada` print it. Take it through /solodev-mission; I approve the spec as soon as you present it, and the coder can be this tool.
evals.expected_output: Run in a copy of test/fixture-repo. One spec and plan in the feature folder under `solodev probe`'s state.dir, one gate, an approval line in progress.md, one coder writing the journey test and code, proven red on the base and green on the branch, one fresh review, and a ready, unmerged PR.
expectations: spec.md has @S<n> scenarios and plan.md has a fenced journeys: block with at most 3 journeys
The user saw exactly one gate, and its last question offered the coder options from `solodev probe`
Spec review was skipped (one journey, nothing risky) and the commander said why
`solodev approve` appended the approval line to progress.md before any source file was committed, and the coder choice was logged there
The coder ran as shadow-coder with the solodev-code skill, and `solodev check <slug> --for implement` passed before review
Code review ran in a fresh shadow-reviewer and wrote review.md in the feature folder; no file of the feature folder was committed to the repo
No QA agent started, because plan.md listed no uncovered scenarios
The new module's directory has a README of at most 30 lines naming its entry point, the exported function has a one-line doc comment, and no documenter ran
`solodev check <slug> --for done` passed and the commander, not a shadow, marked the PR ready; nothing was merged
Every report started with a progress bar, and each delegation was announced in one line before it started
